title: Teradyne Robotics Revenue Jumps 33% on AI Demand
summary: Teradyne reported second-quarter 2026 results on July 28, with robotics revenue of $100 million, up 33% year over year. The segment covers Universal Robots' collaborative arms and Mobile Industrial Robots' AMRs. Management tied the quarter to AI-driven demand across semiconductor test, product test and robotics, with robotics growth concentrated in e-commerce, logistics and electronics manufacturing — notably assembly of data-centre equipment.
whyItMatters: Collaborative-arm and AMR sales are a slow-moving industrial indicator, so a 33% year-over-year jump is a demand signal rather than a funding-round headline. It also shows where physical AI revenue is actually landing today: not in humanoids, but in the arms and mobile robots building the data centres that train the models.
